source.title: ProSelfLC: Progressive Self Label Correction for Training Robust Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Xinshao Wang; Hua Yang; E. Kodirov; D. Clifton; N. Robertson

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the relevant findings.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures fitting of incorrect/noisy labels and its relationship to generalization, refining the broad claim with experiments on partially corrupted labels. It does not run fully random labels or unstructured inputs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports wrong-label fitting and correction dynamics for CIFAR-100 with 40% asymmetric noise, including the comparison of ProSelfLC and other target-modification methods. These results bear on V4 and V6. The clean-label and standard/noisy test-accuracy comparisons do not measure the random-label fitting claim. The Arpit et al. claim about learning meaningful patterns before fitting noise is cited as prior work and as motivation, not tested here.
record.test_reason: The study reports standard cross-entropy test accuracy across increasing synthetic corruption rates and directly measures noisy-label fitting under ProSelfLC. These bear on V4 in a new setting. The real-patterns-before-noise proposition motivates the method but is not independently established by the supplied temporal results.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that ProSelfLC progressively and adaptively uses self predictions to improve target structure and correct noisy semantic labels, outperforming the compared methods in clean and noisy settings. They argue that rewarding appropriately defined low-entropy predictions can improve generalization. Learning meaningful patterns before fitting noise is a cited premise, rather than a separately established conclusion here.
record.recipe_differences: This paper proposes and evaluates progressive self label correction, a target-modification training method, rather than reproducing the original random-label experiments. It uses partial synthetic and real-world label noise.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported label-correction and accuracy results vary with label-noise type and rate; the authors report that a smaller B performs better at higher noise rates. Figure 2 compares trust-score schemes, with the best fixed trust value selected for display.

fits_no_version.finding: ProSelfLC outperforms CCE on clean-test accuracy under partial synthetic label corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Progressive self label correction improves robustness to label noise relative to standard cross-entropy training.

record.problems: The relevant wrong-label fitting results are limited to CIFAR-100 with 40% asymmetric label noise and are described via referenced figures; no experiment uses fully random labels, and no uncertainty estimates are given for these results. The paper's claim about learning meaningful patterns before fitting noise is cited from prior work rather than directly tested as a real-label-versus-random-label comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other standard-setting and noisy-label test accuracies compare label-modification methods, but do not measure the versions' named random-label fitting behavior; Table 5 lists hyperparameter results rather than a separate random-label experiment.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error under that labeling, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus real labels and convergence-time changes across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

The full corruption range through completely random labels and chance-level test performance; perfect training-set fitting by standard CCE is not established in the supplied readable text. ProSelfLC's fitting measurements concern modified learning targets.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.

An independently demonstrated temporal ordering of real-pattern learning before noisy-label memorization. Endpoint fitting and correction rates do not establish this ordering; the proposition is cited as a design premise.

missing.what: Dedicated standard-CCE rows for the clean baseline and corruption sweep. Clean accuracy is 69.0%; asymmetric r=0.2/0.3 gives 66.6%/63.4%; symmetric r=0.2/0.4/0.6 gives 58.0%/50.1%/37.9%. These results bear directly on V4's test-degradation component, even though the record dismisses other accuracy comparisons.

Figures 3–4 include comparator wrong-label-fitting dynamics, including standard CCE, that are absent from the record's discussion of omitted dynamics. Their numerical trajectories cannot be recovered from the supplied text; obtain readable curves before assigning training-fit or temporal-order verdicts.

record.verdict_notes: The study is neither original source. No V6 verdict is warranted from the readable evidence. The asymmetric corruption parameter affects two of five fine classes within each coarse class; it must not be reported as the overall fraction of corrupted training labels.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment with completely random training labels or a direct measure of training error and test error at chance under random labels.
No comparison of training time to fit random labels versus true labels or sweep of corruption fractions measuring convergence time.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiment.

The paper tests 40% asymmetric label noise on CIFAR-100 and describes results on noisy-label subsets, but does not sweep corruption continuously from none to all or establish steadily rising test error toward chance across that full range.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout or data augmentation prevent fitting fully random labels, or whether removing them makes true-label generalization poor.

The paper examines fitting wrong labels and correction during training under 40% asymmetric label noise, but does not compare completely random labels against real labels as separate training conditions.

rows.subject: ProSelfLC
rows.operation_detail: Trained with ProSelfLC on CIFAR-100 with 40% asymmetric label noise; analyzed wrong-label fitting on the noisy subset.
rows.measure: Fraction of noisy labels fitted during training, as described in Appendix B.
rows.locator: Appendix B, Discussion on wrongly confident predictions and model calibration; Figure 3b cited
rows.note: Authors state ProSelfLC fits noisy labels least, and that a few noisy labels are memorised with high confidence. This is wrong-label fitting under partial asymmetric corruption, not fully random labels.
rows.check: The approximately 12% wrong-label fitting is correct, but does not establish the temporal ordering in V6. Describe the condition as asymmetric r=0.4: Section 5.2 explicitly says the overall corruption fraction is smaller than r. ProSelfLC changes learning targets, so this is a qualification for that intervention.

relationships.condition: Standard CCE, ResNet-44, CIFAR-100; clean labels and increasing symmetric or asymmetric corruption
relationships.reason: Supports the test-degradation component only: accuracy falls from 69.0% clean to 58.0%, 50.1%, and 37.9% under symmetric r=0.2/0.4/0.6, and to 66.6%, 63.4%, and 59.5% under asymmetric r=0.2/0.3/0.4. R4 records the last value; the remaining baseline results come directly from Tables 4–5 and need dedicated rows.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell from 69.0% clean to 58.0%, 50.1%, and 37.9% at symmetric rates 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6, and to 66.6%, 63.4%, and 59.5% at asymmetric rates 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4.

relationships.condition: ProSelfLC target modification, ResNet-44, CIFAR-100, asymmetric r=0.4
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show approximately 12% fitting and 88% correction of noisy annotations, so perfect fitting of supplied labels does not extend to this correction intervention.
relationships.display_finding: Approximately 12% of noisy annotations were fitted and 88% were corrected.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: ProSelfLC corrects about 88% of noisy labels but still fits around 12%; its reported clean-test accuracy under this partial-noise condition does not establish perfect fitting or the full smooth trend (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that noisy-label fitting is reduced and correction occurs, but a few noisy labels are still memorised; it does not test the cited real-before-random comparison directly (R1–R2).
